topic: Resolve the sharp computational minimax frontier for the direct treatment effect under q=2 arbitrary neighborhood interference on known d-regular networks. Define R_2(G) as the infimum worst-case MSE over every assignment law and measurable estimator, and kappa_DTE(d) as the best uniform factor with which a randomized polynomial-time algorithm outputs an implementable design-estimator plus a valid upper risk certificate. Under the Unique Games Conjecture together with NP not contained in BPP, prove kappa_DTE(d)=d^(1/2+o(1)): for every epsilon>0 no d^(1/2-epsilon) approximation works on all sufficiently large d, while a polynomial Conflict Graph Design procedure achieves C*sqrt(d). The lower theorem must be a two-sided value-preserving reduction from regular independent set to the special two-layer DTE maximal-independent-set game, with a low-risk YES design and a high-risk NO Le Cam or dual certificate; the published one-sided alpha lower bound, hardness of a proxy, and hardness for one estimator do not suffice. Output the realizable randomization, modified Horvitz-Thompson estimator, and computable upper certificate, and use Fatemi-Zheleva CauseIS as the consumer whose MIS-based DTE benchmarking changes.

open_problems.open_problem: Does q=2 DTE minimax risk on known d-regular interference networks admit no randomized polynomial-time d^(1/2-epsilon)-approximation, for every epsilon>0, under UGC and NP not contained in BPP, while Conflict Graph Design attains a computably certified O(sqrt(d)) approximation?

source_refs.claim: Conjecture 2 states d^(1/2-epsilon) hardness for approximating d-regular DTE minimax risk; computationally efficient minimax risk is left open.
source_refs.author: Vardis Kandiros, Christopher Harshaw, Fredrik Sävje

source_refs.claim: Under UGC, maximum independent set in bounded-degree graphs is hard to approximate within O(d/log^2 d), but this does not itself reduce to statistical minimax risk.
source_refs.author: Per Austrin, Subhash Khot, Muli Safra

source_refs.claim: Conflict Graph Design supplies a realizable randomization, modified Horvitz-Thompson estimator, q=2 risk bound, exposure probabilities, and conservative variance certificate.
source_refs.author: Vardis Kandiros, Charilaos Pipis, Constantinos Daskalakis, Christopher Harshaw

source_refs.excerpt: Develop a bounded-degree compression theorem with an explicit algorithm, certificate size, and approximation ratio
Finite programs can be exponentially large; polynomial-time computation and graph compression remain open.
The all-rule lower bound, including its required nuisance-rich indistinguishability construction, remains open.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Kandiros, Harshaw, and Sävje prove only separated statistical upper and lower bounds and leave the d^(1/2-epsilon) computational claim as Conjecture 2. Austrin-Khot-Safra hardness cannot simply be applied to the published independence-number lower bound because R_2(G) is an implicit game over assignment laws and all measurable estimators: a reduction must preserve both directions, constructing a low-risk YES design and a design-uniform high-risk NO Le Cam or dual witness. The prior-proposal bank independently records that exact finite saddles can be exponentially large, asks for bounded-degree compression with an explicit algorithm and certificate, and identifies nuisance-rich all-rule indistinguishability as the missing lower-bound step. The upper side must connect the realizable Conflict Graph randomization and modified HT estimator to an ex ante polynomially computable risk certificate relative to unrestricted minimax value, not merely optimize a graph proxy or analyze a fixed estimator.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A matching pair of theorems defining kappa_DTE(d): a randomized value-preserving regular-MIS-to-two-layer-DTE reduction proving d^(1/2-epsilon) inapproximability for R_2(G), and a polynomial Conflict Graph Design algorithm outputting an assignment law, modified HT estimator, and valid certificate at most C sqrt(d) R_2(G).

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the exact minimax benchmark, isolates the sqrt(d) statistical gap on regular graphs, and ends with the computational conjecture that the new work would resolve.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Network designs lack a universal benchmark -> conflict graphs encode the joint design-estimation problem -> regular-graph DTE has a sqrt(d) gap between accessible bounds -> determine the computationally attainable minimax frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the UGC completeness-soundness reduction for bounded-degree independent set, including degree regularization and preservation of the independent-set value gap.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired lower theorem must import its regular independent-set gap while proving that the induced two-layer DTE statistical game preserves both YES and NO values.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt design-dependent least-favourable outcome mixtures, Le Cam testing bounds, and reduction of designs to distributions over maximal independent sets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These are the published lower-bound tools that range over every assignment law and estimator, exactly the quantifiers required by R_2(G).

method_exemplars.technique: Use importance-ordered conflict resolution, modified HT weighting by closed-form desired-exposure probabilities, operator-norm variance control, and conservative variance estimation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This machinery gives the implementable upper procedure and certificate; the missing proof is its uniform approximation ratio relative to unrestricted minimax value.

open_problems.open_problem: Can q=2 DTE minimax risk for the special two-layer conflict graph be represented, up to universal constants, by an explicit primal-dual game over distributions on maximal independent sets with efficiently checkable dual lower-risk certificates?

source_refs.claim: The paper proves conflict-graph sufficiency and that maximal independent sets suffice, but leaves the graph functional implicit and asks for an exact characterization.
source_refs.author: Vardis Kandiros, Christopher Harshaw, Fredrik Sävje

open_problems.why_unsolved: The current characterization still contains the original minimization over designs and estimators; the q=2 conflict-graph functional is not explicitly constructed. Available lower summaries use induced independence numbers or local degree, while available upper summaries use spectral radius and vertex deletion, and both extremes can be tight even among d-regular graphs. The missing step is to eliminate the measurable estimator and potential-outcome adversary in favor of a finite convex game whose design marginals respect the special two-layer maximal-independent-set structure; duality must then yield witnesses strong enough for NO instances rather than recycling the one-sided independence-number lower bound.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit finite-dimensional primal program for R_2(G), or a constant-equivalent surrogate, together with a strong-duality theorem and a dual feasible certificate whose objective lower-bounds the worst-case MSE of every assignment law and measurable estimator.

writing_exemplar.why: Its narrative moves directly from conflict-graph sufficiency to the unresolved need for an explicit description of the hidden graph functional.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Minimax risk depends only on incompatibility of exposures -> maximal independent sets encode maximally informative assignments -> existing graph summaries separate on regular families -> expose the hidden game and its dual certificate

method_exemplars.technique: Use conflict-graph sufficiency and the restriction from arbitrary assignments to probability measures over maximal independent sets as the primal reduction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is precisely the structural reduction that a primal-dual representation must make explicit for the two-layer DTE graph.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt exact joint design-estimator minimax analysis via a vertex prior, Hilbert-space projection, and a midpoint-differenced Horvitz-Thompson attaining strategy.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It eliminates estimators in an analogous finite-population squared-error game; the changed proof step is replacing freely selectable samples by conflict-constrained exposure sets.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the quadratic-form and operator-norm expression for modified-HT risk under conflict-constrained randomization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its risk matrix is a natural primal upper object against which a new dual lower certificate could be paired.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the worst-case q=2 approximation ratio of Fatemi-Zheleva CauseIS to unrestricted DTE minimax risk on d-regular networks, and can an implementable weighted CauseIS variant achieve a certified ratio or must explicit regular graph families exhibit a polynomial separation?

source_refs.claim: CauseIS selects a maximum independent set, randomizes its vertices between treatment and control, and evaluates DTE performance empirically under a peer-cancellation argument.
source_refs.author: Zahra Fatemi, Elena Zheleva

source_refs.claim: Universal DTE minimax risk optimizes jointly over all assignment laws and estimators; earlier independent-set work restricts the procedure or adds outcome assumptions.
source_refs.author: Vardis Kandiros, Christopher Harshaw, Fredrik Sävje

source_refs.claim: Independent-set design can control focal treatments and interference exposures, but its theory does not characterize universal q=2 DTE minimax risk.
source_refs.author: Chencheng Cai, Xu Zhang, Edoardo M. Airoldi

open_problems.why_unsolved: CauseIS optimizes the cardinality of one independent set and benchmarks simulated error, whereas R_2(G) optimizes over distributions on all realizable exposures and every estimator under arbitrary neighborhood interference with only a second-moment restriction. A large MIS can coexist with unfavorable exposure probabilities or correlations, so the independence number alone cannot certify worst-case MSE. The technique-derived destination is a universal-risk audit of CauseIS: the first proof step must replace its bystander-cancellation argument and difference comparison by exact desired-exposure probabilities and a worst-case quadratic-risk or Le Cam analysis. The 2026 minimax paper cites independent-set designs but does not evaluate CauseIS's approximation ratio.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving the sharp asymptotic supremum over d-regular G of Risk_2(CauseIS,G)/R_2(G), accompanied either by a polynomial realizable weighted-MIS randomization, modified HT estimator, and computable certificate attaining that order, or by explicit regular graph and potential-outcome families proving the separation.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the applied DTE contamination problem and presents CauseIS as the concrete MIS-based design whose benchmark would change.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Peer spillovers contaminate ordinary DTE comparisons -> independent experimental units remove direct cross-arm interference -> CauseIS operationalizes this with an MIS -> determine its performance against the universal design-based minimax benchmark

method_exemplars.technique: Use the universal design-estimator minimax definition, graph-specific Le Cam lower bounds, and regular-family tightness constructions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies both the denominator R_2(G) and the adversarial proof machinery needed for a genuine approximation ratio.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the modified HT estimator with analytically computable exposure probabilities and an observable conservative variance certificate.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A certifiable CauseIS repair must solve exactly the exposure-probability and worst-case-risk deficiencies absent from its current empirical benchmark.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt independent-set plus auxiliary-set assignment that separately controls focal treatment and interference exposure.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest structurally richer MIS randomization from which a weighted CauseIS variant could be derived before proving its universal-risk guarantee.

open_problems.open_problem: Is the computable conflict-graph upper-risk certificate for a modified Horvitz-Thompson direct-effect estimator exact or uniformly constant-factor sharp over bounded q=2 potential-outcome schedules?

source_refs.excerpt: Investigate whether V_env is sharp or constant-factor sharp as a worst-case bounded-outcome variance envelope

open_problems.why_unsolved: The source review identifies the generic obstacle for observable graph-only certificates: absolute-value domination produces a valid envelope, but a bounded least-favourable schedule may be unable to align all covariance signs and centering constraints simultaneously. For the destination one-mode DTE problem, the first proof step changes from the bipartite Hájek covariance expansion to the Conflict Graph Design modified-HT MSE expansion. Until its spectral certificate is compared with the exact bounded-table sign maximization, an algorithmic upper bound need not certify proximity to causal minimax risk.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving the optimal universal ratio between the computable conflict-graph certificate and exact worst-case DTE MSE, either by constructing least-favourable bounded schedules or by an explicit graph family proving a strict gap, together with an attaining certified design.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames DTE estimation through target-specific conflicts and makes the graph certificate the operational object.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: DTE exposure events conflict under arbitrary neighborhoods -> Conflict Graph Design yields a realizable modified-HT procedure -> determine whether its observable spectral risk bound measures the true worst-case causal risk

method_exemplars.technique: Represent valid conservative interference-variance bounds by admissible quadratic domination and optimize them through convex programming.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The open object is precisely the sharpness factor of a computable conservative quadratic certificate for a causal estimator.

method_exemplars.technique: Compare conflict-graph upper and lower functionals for unrestricted minimax risk.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its lower functional supplies the natural benchmark against which certificate sharpness must be tested.

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze the modified Horvitz-Thompson estimator under conflict-graph randomization and derive its spectral MSE guarantee.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the exact estimator and certificate whose worst-case bounded-schedule sharpness is unresolved.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the exact or asymptotic implementability gap between an ideal covariance or SDP relaxation of q=2 DTE risk on d-regular conflict graphs and the best realizable randomized assignment law?

source_refs.excerpt: The exact zero/positive-loss frontier r_star is deliberately left as the honest open object

open_problems.why_unsolved: The source construction reduces a symmetric causal design objective to an active-set SOCP and compares the elliptope with realizable plus/minus-one second moments, but its exact contact strata remain open even on that family. The DTE destination replaces two-block orbit symmetry by an arbitrary d-regular conflict graph. The first proof step that changes is the covariance-image reduction: one must identify the relevant cut-polytope face for target-exposure assignments before any Gaussian or dependent rounding loss can be translated into causal MSE.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp integrality-gap characterization, or matching upper and lower degree-order bounds, together with a polynomial-time rounding algorithm that outputs a realizable DTE randomization and a valid post-rounding risk certificate.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates causal design through worst-case MSE optimization over assignment covariances and makes realizability the central boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Interference-aware worst-case MSE admits a tractable covariance relaxation -> relaxed covariances need not come from binary assignments -> quantify and algorithmically close the realizability gap for DTE conflict graphs

method_exemplars.technique: Characterize symmetric Bernoulli correlation matrices as an affine image of the cut polytope and prove covariance realizability geometrically.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The first required object is the realizable covariance image of the DTE assignment-law class.

method_exemplars.technique: Produce an explicitly realizable graph-aware randomization and couple it to modified Horvitz-Thompson risk analysis.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the causal estimator and implementable benchmark needed to convert a covariance integrality gap into a DTE risk gap.

literature_map:
1. Kandiros, Harshaw, and Sävje (2026, arXiv:2608.04909) introduce unrestricted joint design-estimator minimax risk under arbitrary neighborhood interference and make the conflict graph sufficient for the risk.
2. Their q=2 d-regular DTE bounds leave a sqrt(d) multiplicative gap, with separate regular families attaining the d/n and sqrt(d)/n extremes and random regular graphs lying near d/n.
3. The same paper's Conjecture 2 is exactly d^(1/2-epsilon) hardness for DTE risk approximation; it offers independent-set evidence but no value-preserving statistical reduction.
4. Kandiros, Pipis, Daskalakis, and Harshaw (2024, arXiv:2411.10908) provide Conflict Graph Design, a realizable importance-ordered randomization, modified HT estimator, q=2 variance control, and conservative inference.
5. Austrin, Khot, and Safra (2011, Theory of Computing, doi:10.4086/toc.2011.v007a003) give UGC hardness O(d/log^2 d) for bounded-degree independent set, the natural donor gap theorem.
6. Fatemi and Zheleva (2020 workshop; 2023 Frontiers in Big Data, doi:10.3389/fdata.2023.1128649) make MIS the operational core of CauseIS, but validate it through peer cancellation and simulation rather than universal minimax risk.
7. Cai, Zhang, and Airoldi (ICLR 2024, arXiv:2312.04026) show that independent-set designs can jointly manipulate treatment and spillover exposures under added structure, suggesting a richer MIS design space than CauseIS.
8. Aronow and Samii (2017, Annals of Applied Statistics, arXiv:1305.6156) establish the general exposure-mapping and inverse-probability framework, randomization variance estimation, consistency, and local-dependence asymptotic normality.
9. Hudgens and Halloran (2008, JASA, doi:10.1198/016214508000000292) supply the foundational design-based direct and spillover estimands under interference.
10. Ugander et al. (2013, arXiv:1305.6979) and Ugander-Yin (2023, Journal of Causal Inference, arXiv:2009.02297) develop graph-cluster randomization and efficiently estimated exposure probabilities, primarily for GATE.
11. Leung (2022, Econometrica, doi:10.3982/ECTA17841) supplies IPW limit theory and network-HAC inference under approximate neighborhood interference, but not the finite-population computational design frontier.
12. Basse and Airoldi (2018, Biometrika, doi:10.1093/biomet/asy036) optimize designs relative to a working outcome model, illustrating the distinction between model-assisted and unrestricted minimax optimality.
13. Aronow and Lopatto (2026, arXiv:2605.20572) exactly solve a related joint finite-population design-estimator minimax problem using a vertex prior, Hilbert projection, and midpoint-differenced HT estimator.
14. Gandhi, Khuller, and Srinivasan (2004, Journal of Algorithms) and Saha et al. (2015, SDM) underlie polynomial vertex/eigenvalue-deletion approximation, but optimize an upper-risk proxy rather than R_2(G).
15. The central tension is live: implementable conflict-resolution designs and observable certificates exist, and MIS hardness exists, but no published theorem connects them by the required two-sided value-preserving reduction over all designs and measurable estimators.
